schemes.OAuth2Assertion.description: "Authenticate as the employee using the `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` grant in the OAuth2 protocol,
with an assertion whose subject is `urn:remote-api:employee:employment:<employment_id>`.

OpenAPI has no flow type for this grant, so it is declared as a client credentials flow. Request the token
from the token URL with this grant type and a signed assertion, not with `client_credentials`.

Remote must allow the integration to act on behalf of users, and the integration must manage the employee's company.
Remote can also limit an integration to grants that carry a user's consent, such as the Authorization Code flow;
this grant is then refused.

The same grant also issues company-manager tokens: see `OAuth2CompanyManagerAssertion`.
"

schemes.OAuth2CompanyManagerAssertion.description: "Authenticate as a company manager using the `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` grant in the OAuth2 protocol,
with an assertion whose subject is `urn:remote-api:company-manager:user:<user_id>`, where `<user_id>` is the
company manager's Remote `user_id`. Each user belongs to one company.

OpenAPI has no flow type for this grant, so it is declared as a client credentials flow. Request the token
from the token URL with this grant type and a signed assertion, not with `client_credentials`.

Remote must allow the integration to act on behalf of users, and the integration must manage the user's company.
Remote can also limit an integration to grants that carry a user's consent, such as the Authorization Code flow;
this grant is then refused.

The token acts as that company manager, and is accepted wherever a company manager's token from the
Authorization Code flow is.
"
